incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for service=private-controlplane severity=high — oncall=Sara L :rotating_light:
pagerduty: INC-5412 created for customer=acme-corp — missing heartbeat from private control plane agent in us-west-2 VPC. Impact: control plane APIs returning 502s for management calls.
Sara L: acked — taking ownership. I see the PD page, starting triage. tagging @Hamid R for infra help.
Hamid R: on it. quick question — is this isolated to acme-corp or multi-customer?
prod-obs-bot: Alert correlation: 3 similar control-plane heartbeat drops in past 10m across different tenants in us-west-2; however only acme-corp's agent shows full disconnect.
Jen K: adding context — acme-corp has private deployment with on-prem agent + VPC peering to our control plane. Their agent last heartbeat 2026-03-14T15:22:31Z.
Sara L: I can reach our control-plane LB from inside the VPC via the console check? running quick probe.
Kevin M: I'll try to reach the agent from our maintenance host over the peering. Sharing commands:
```
# from maintenance jump
nc -vz 10.2.15.8 443
curl -sS -I https://controlplane.redwood-private.internal/health
```
Sara L: probe shows 502 at control plane edge for that tenant ID.
Luis (Support): Customer reports management UI shows "Connection lost" but app traffic is fine — data plane unaffected. They are worried about plugin config changes not going through.
Hamid R: checking routing tables and Security Groups for the VPC peering. Nothing obvious. Checking BGP flaps logs on our transit GW.
prod-obs-bot: BGP session flapped with peer acme-transit at 15:20:47 UTC — 2x flaps in 7m.
Sara L: OK that explains intermittent control plane reachability. Next steps: 1) keep customer informed; 2) escalate to network oncall if flaps continue; 3) fail open configs to avoid management writes blocking data plane.
Hamid R: I'm escalating to network oncall @Kevin M — please take a look at the transit box.
Kevin M: got it. I see a kernel crash on the transit peer around 15:20:40, interface reset. I'm pulling logs and will try to reboot the peer process if remote config allows.
Jen K: While Kevin works the transit, Sara can you run a short mitigation to reduce customer impact? Suggest toggling control-plane write lock for acme-corp to allow config syncs to be queued instead of failing. Command:
```
# pseudo-config
redwoodctl tenant config set acme-corp --writes=queue --reason "incident INC-5412"
```
Sara L: applied write queue flag, verified via API: tenant config writes now accept and are queued. Not ideal but avoids customer-facing errors for management UI.
Luis (Support): Just told customer we've queued management changes and are investigating network flaps. They appreciate the update.
prod-obs-bot: Notification: Network oncall Kevin M acknowledged escalation.
Kevin M: performed soft-restart of transit peer process, BGP session re-established at 15:26:02. Monitoring for stability.
Hamid R: monitoring shows heartbeats resumed at 15:27:10 for acme-corp agent.
Sara L: can confirm control plane health OK for tenant — management API 200s and queued writes draining.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-5412 marked: mitigated — not closed. Owner=Sara L, action=network restart and tenant write-queue applied.
Sara L: prepping post-incident notes and will schedule follow-up RCA with network team and support. Assigning follow-up ticket NET-298 for transit peer kernel issue.
Jen K: thanks all. I'll draft the customer-facing update for tomorrow morning summarizing mitigation and next steps. :white_check_mark:
Kevin M: leaving a sticky note in the transit peer's runbook about kernel upgrade/patch to prevent recurrence.
Sara L: handing back to followups — I am off after 16:00 UTC, please pick up RCA items.
Luis (Support): customer acknowledged and happy with workaround for now.
Sara L: closing live triage thread.
